Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Unity Insurance Group Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Unity Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; David Kim, Chief Investment Officer; Jennifer Lee, Chief Operating Officer; Robert Hayes, Chief Claims Officer; and Emily Wong, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Unity Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by reliable dividend payments signaling our shareholder commitment, the positive impact of pricing changes on premium volume amid market hardening, favorable realized and unrealized gains and losses on investments, robust new business production volume in both premiums and policies, the effectiveness of our reinsurance program in mitigating volatility, strong reinsurance recoveries received and expected, attractive investment income yields from our diversified portfolio, and improving loss ratio trends through better claims frequency and severity management. Our commitment to innovation and customer service continues to drive our success.

Michael Chen, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. As Sarah mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $475 million, or $1.42 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included resilient underwriting margins, higher investment returns, disciplined expense management, growth in earned premiums, favorable prior year development, and strong free cash flow generation. Our combined ratio was 92.4%. Investment income for the quarter was $650 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with adjusted book value per share at $68.45 and excess capital of $2.8 billion above our targets. Our expense ratio also improved to 28.1%.

Before diving deeper into segment details, let me highlight our dividend payments, which remain a cornerstone of our capital return framework and a clear signal of our financial strength and dedication to shareholders. Unity has increased our common stock dividend for 28 consecutive years, putting us in elite company with peers like Chubb and Travelers in the property and casualty space. Today, our Board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.48 per share, payable on November 15th to shareholders of record as of October 25th. This is a 6.3% increase from the $0.45 per share in Q3 2023, annualizing to $1.92 per share, up from $1.80 last year. Over the past five years, our dividend has grown at a 5.2% CAGR, surpassing the S&P 500 Insurance Index average of 4.1%.

This payout is comfortably covered by our earnings, with Q3 core operating EPS at $1.42, yielding a 34% payout ratio within our 30-40% target. Trailing twelve-month EPS is $5.68, providing 3.4x coverage on a cash flow basis adjusted for catastrophes. Free cash flow hit $1.2 billion this quarter, supported by our 92.4% combined ratio—flat year-over-year despite $450 million in cat losses from Hurricane Helene and California wildfires. Ex-cats, we're at 88.2%, with loss ratios improving 120 basis points to 62.5% via our AI-driven claims platform, which cut cycle times by 25% and leakage by 8%.

This hike aligns with our fortress balance sheet, where adjusted book value grew 7.2% year-over-year. We're returning 85% of deployable capital via dividends and buybacks, including $750 million repurchased year-to-date at $52 per share, accretive by 2.5% to book value. This approach supports growth without the cuts some peers faced, like Hartford in 2022 amid inflation.

Diversified earnings bolster sustainability: North America P&C, 65% of premiums, grew 9% organically with 12% auto rates and 8% commercial, while homeowners earned premiums rose 11% at a 55% loss ratio through RMS and ClimateAi modeling. Investment income jumped 22% year-over-year, with portfolio yield at 4.8% on $45 billion fixed income, 60% investment-grade corporates and munis. Internationally, Asia-Pacific APE grew 15% via unit-linked products like Unity Vitality Flex in Japan and Australia, with 25% ROE offsetting U.S. cats and value of new business margins at 28%. Europe grew 7%, with expense ratio down 50 basis points to 28.1% via robotic process automation.

Tailwinds for 2025 include UnderwriteAI 2.0 for 300 basis points combined ratio gains through telematics pricing across 12 million policyholders, akin to Progressive's Snapshot. January reinsurance renews at mid-90s ceding commissions with 45% cat layer protection up to $2 billion via Swiss Re and RenaissanceRe. Inflation normalizes claims, 10-year Treasury at 4.2% boosts floating-rate returns, projecting $2.9 billion 2025 investment income and 8-10% EPS growth ex-cats at 14-16% ROE. Our $4.5 billion liquidity and stress-tested policy withstand 1-in-200-year cats, unlike yield-chasing peers.

Turning to premium growth, pricing changes significantly influenced volume. Consolidated net written premiums grew 4.2% to $2.8 billion, our ninth straight organic quarter, despite 6.1% earned rate increases—most aggressive since post-Katrina. Policy count rose 1.8% globally, with book-to-bill at 1.05x.

In Personal Lines (55% of premiums), 7.3% hikes—8.2% auto for 12% repair inflation per CCC, 6.5% homeowners for reinsurance and perils—drove 2.4% volume growth via digital channels. Retention hit 88.2%, up 50 basis points, from AI pricing with DriveWise telematics at 92% best-risk retention.

Commercial Lines (35%) averaged 5.8% rates amid competition, flat 0.2% volume prioritizing adequacy; loss ratio improved 210 basis points to 62.4%, combined at 95.6% via RiskOptix ML on ISO data. Specialty (10%) grew 9.1% premiums on 4.5% volume with 12% D&O rates post-CrowdStrike; cyber at $450 million used parametrics.

U.S. (70%) grew 5.1% premiums, 2.6% volume: Florida 9.8%, Texas 7.2%. Europe (20%) 2.3% with UK motor at 4.5%; Asia (10%) 8.7% via usage-based in India with drone underwriting.

Our Profitable Growth Framework, with $150 million in pricing tech including RMS v17.1, shows -0.3x elasticity versus industry -0.6x, aided by 22% Home+Auto bundling. Q4 rates at 5.5%, 2-3% volume growth with GenAI personalization.

On investments, realized gains were $312 million, up 45% year-over-year on $152 billion portfolio at 4.2% book yield, 92% fixed income AA- average. Sales in AFS MBS and corporates harvested 8.2% gains on $2.8 billion short-duration assets, shortening duration to 5.9 years. Credit rotations in energy/financials added $145 million; equities $28 million from JPM and BRK trims. Munis aided tax efficiency; trailing gains $1.1 billion at 3.2% return.

Unrealized losses narrowed to $27 million from $450 million prior, cumulative $2.4 billion AOCI down 18%. Fixed income $2.1 billion mostly long Treasuries/supranationals; convexity swaps avoided OTTI. Equities/alts gained $120 million on 12% equities and $1.2 billion private credit.

U.S. (72%) drove 65% gains; Europe (15%) $45 million sovereigns; Asia (8%) JGBs. Aladdin-powered ALM boosted corporates to 28%, ESG greens; YTD income $1.6 billion up 12%.

Ahead, $200-250 million quarterly realized gains, $6.2-6.5 billion full-year income; alternatives to 10% by 2025.

New business production hit $2.8 billion APE, up 18% year-over-year and 7% sequentially—strongest since Q4 2021—with 1.2 million policies, up 22%. P&C $1.5 billion APE/850,000 policies: auto $950 million (+28%) via ApexDrive UBI at 40% penetration, cutting acquisition 15%; homeowners $450 million (+20%) with Zillow embeds. Life/Annuities $850 million/280,000: term $500 million (+15%) via SI engine at 75% approvals; UL/indexed $350 million. Group $450 million/70,000: voluntary $300 million (+18%), cyber $100 million (+50%).

North America 72%/$2.0 billion (+20%); EMEA $500 million (+12%); APAC $300 million (+25%) via Jio micro-life. Digital 55%, embedded $200 million up 60%. Outpaced industry 11%; PVNBP $11.5-12 billion implies 16% value growth.

Our reinsurance program optimized RAROC, retaining $250 million per risk/occurrence on U.S. portfolio up to $1.2 billion NPML; ceded 28% GWP or $4.2 billion YTD. Cost 12%, down 50 basis points via RenaissanceRe, PartnerRe. Recoveries $2.1 billion on $1.8 billion ceded premiums, 117% ratio.

Gross combined 102.5% to net 92.3%, 10.2-point benefit ex-cats 88.7%. U.S. 85% coverage on $850 million Hurricane Elena; Europe 75% on $300 million Storm Bertha with ILW; Asia 92% Typhoon Kai. UnityCat 2.0 improved projections 18%; $400 million cat bonds. Solvency 180% post-reinsurance.

Reinsurance recoveries received $1.2 billion Q3, up 25% year-over-year; YTD $3.1 billion or 62% gross cats. P&C $1.05 billion: $650 million Beryl, $280 million wildfires. Casualty $120 million, L&H $30 million. Lag down to 75 days via AI/RMS; net loss ratio 52.4% from gross 58.2%.

North America 72%, Europe 18%, Asia 8%. Expected $850 million 2024 + $400 million priors at 68% cession on $5.8 billion cats; Milton $450 million ultimate. Renewals 100% capacity, 2-4% pricing; $350 million cat bonds, parametrics. Recovery Hub improved reserves 15%.

Investment yield 4.25%, up 140 basis points year-over-year on $180 billion portfolio; TTM 4.18% beating Barclays 3.9%. Income $1.92 billion up 22%, 28% pre-tax operating. New book 5.35%; fixed 78%/4.40% (IG corporates 5.10%, MBS 4.85%); equities 12%/6.20%; alts 8%/7.80%.

Duration 5.8 years; 92% IG. U.S. 4.45%, Europe 3.90%, Asia 4.75%. Aladdin stress-testing, 35% ESG; $5 billion private credit.

Loss ratios trended to 61.8% YTD, down 140 basis points; accident ex-cat 59.4%/-220 bps; Q3 62.5% beating 64% guide. Personal 60.2%/-310 bps: auto frequency 4.1% growth, severity +9.8%/$28,400 on repairs; homeowners flat frequency, +7.5% severity. Commercial 64.1%/-90 bps: frequency -3.2%, severity +8.7%.

Cats $320 million/2.4 points; PYD +1.6. UBI 35% penetration -18% frequency; AI triage -25% cycles/8% leakage; rates 9.2%. Q4 60-62% ex-cat.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our property and casualty lines. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including advanced AI underwriting tools like UnderwriteAI 2.0 and dynamic pricing strategies tied to telematics and catastrophe modeling.

David Kim: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income corporates, private credit, and ESG-labeled assets, maintaining a high-quality profile while capturing yield enhancements.

Robert Hayes: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including AI adjudication and triage platforms that have reduced processing times by 25% and severity leakage by 8%. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times and improved claims resolution rates, contributing to loss ratio improvements.

Emily Wong: We are making significant investments in technology to enhance our operations and improve the customer experience. Our new DriveWise and RiskOptix platforms, powered by GenAI and integrated with partners like RMS, are expected to drive significant efficiencies and cost savings through better risk selection and personalized pricing.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the dividend sustainability given cat volatility?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, John. As Michael detailed, our dividend is backed by 3.4x coverage, $1.2 billion free cash flow, and a $4.5 billion liquidity buffer stress-tested for 1-in-200-year events. Diversified streams like Asia growth and 4.8% yields ensure we maintain 28-year increases.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of pricing changes on premium volume outlook?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Maria. Pricing at 6.1% drove 4.2% NWP growth with 1.8% volume, elasticity -0.3x. Q4 5.5% rates, 2-3% volume as tech like GenAI rolls out, positioning mid-teens EPS.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Patel: What is the expected impact of regulatory changes on your underwriting strategy?

Lisa Patel: Regulatory scrutiny like PRA in UK has us moderating motor rates to 4.5%, but analytics and LexisNexis fraud detection sustain 1.1% volume. We're adapting with parametric innovations for compliance and growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Can you elaborate on the expected benefits of the new technology platforms?

Emily Wong: Absolutely. Platforms like UnderwriteAI 2.0 and Recovery Optimization Hub improve risk selection 15%, cat projections 18%, and cycles 25%, targeting 300 bps combined ratio gains and sub-60% loss ratios by 2026.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Kim with BlackRock. Please go ahead.

Robert Kim: On reinsurance effectiveness, how does it factor into 2025 renewals?

Michael Chen: Our program delivered 10.2-point combined ratio benefits, 61% NPML reduction. 2025 flat-to-5% pricing with parametrics and $1 billion sidecars positions us strongly amid ample $105 billion alternative capital.

Operator: Our next question is a follow-up from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Regarding investment gains, any shift in unrealized outlook?

David Kim: With yields peaking, unrealizeds inflect positive H2; we're trimming duration to 5.5 years, scaling alts to 12% for sustained 4.0%+ yields.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] That concludes today's questions.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Unity Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
